column1: # What a change can break: the one map of the CI workflow and of `scripts/ci.sh affected`.
# `=NAME<TAB>ERE` names a group of job names of scripts/ci.sh (`scripts/ci.sh --plan`). Any other row is `PATH<TAB>JOBS`: PATH is an ERE over a changed file,
# JOBS an ERE over job names in which {NAME} stands for a group and \N for a group of PATH; `-` means no job (the file is mapped, nothing runs), `.` every job. A file
# takes the union of the rows it matches. A file that no row matches runs every job. The names `gh:sqlite`, `gh:mariadb`, `gh:replication`, `gh:macos` and `gh:musl` are the

# workflow jobs that are not in scripts/ci.sh, and `gh:f1` the run of the Format 1.0 shards (SIFT_FORMAT=1) of a pull request. `scripts/ci.sh --selftest` fails when a tracked file matches no row or a job is in no group, so a new
# test or file is never left out silently. A dispatch and the release check run every job: this map only picks what a push runs.
# A row whose JOBS start with `fast:` is read only by the fast tier of a pull request (`scripts/ci.sh affected --github`, `fastjobs`): a file it matches runs
# the regression tests of its own area there, not of the whole stack above it; the push to main and a dispatch use the rows below, which run the stack.
# groups (a job may be in several: the stack col, agg and table is one chain of code, so a change of one runs the groups above it)
# the format compatibility tiers: Format 1 beside the default Format 2.0, and the upgrade from a v5 cluster (scripts/ci/jobs.sh, format_checks)
# the search the other areas call
# the lanes of scripts/plangate.sh, each at 30000 and 250000 rows
# what the fast tier of a pull request runs besides the tests of the area: the proof of the coverage table and the emulated isolation tests (a few seconds each)
# the areas of scripts/fast-gate.sh the performance ones do not name: the column index (src/col, unless another area owns the file) and the SQL surface
# the whole build and every harness: a change here can break anything
# the CI machinery: it runs every job, and builds nothing the focused performance gate measures
# the fast tier: the tests of the area of a source file (the stack above it, and the other versions, run on the push to main)

# the cost model: a constant or a scale of the planner's prices moves plans of every area (the unit scale of the scan turned agg_topn_plan_keys red), so a change of these files runs every regression test and the plan gates, in the fast tier too
# the column format constants (the minor a build writes): the upgrade tests state the formats they expect
# the harness of one job selects the jobs that run it (`scripts/ci.sh --selftest` fails when it misses one)
# nothing the jobs build or run: release, packaging, benchmarks, documentation, tools, the other workflows

# the quick tier runs the scaling gate only for a change of what the geometry of a unit or a page depends on (the files that name SIFT_SB_SHIFT, the format and page headers: scripts/check-scaling-triggers.sh keeps this row whole); every col or agg change reaches it in the nightly
# the focus table and its generator: read by `scripts/ci.sh affected --focus` only (a local shortcut; CI runs the jobs of the map above)
# the landing script: run by people, by no job
# Focused performance uses the groups above; shared build/SQL cover every group. {perf} marks what cannot change the extension it builds twice
# (the gate, its selector, the CI machinery): identical builds measure only noise, so they select nothing (the nightly run still measures everything).
# {ci} marks the jobs a path can break but not slow: the tests are not built into the extension, and the SiftAgg code is not on the path of the storage cases
# (no grouped query, no table source scan; the aggregate cases read the table through it), so the aggregate stack above it is correctness-only for the gate.

# The areas of scripts/perf/gate.py: `scripts/perf-select.py` reads this map as `ci.sh affected` does and gives each changed path the canaries and the slice of scripts/plangate.sh of the area it can move.

# An area is a `{perf_AREA}` row; a path that names none (a core file, a path no row maps) runs the smoke canaries, and a row names the group that can change it only: a path that serves two areas names both.
# the weights of the tiers and the scratch of the jobs, read by scripts/ci.sh only to cut the shards and to schedule (the jobs run are those of the map above)
# the Alpine (musl) build has no GNU IFUNC: `.` (the build, src/core/) runs it; these are what only it reads
